dashboard_0.title: Page purpose
dashboard_0.body: View live task, asset, finding and resource summaries. Statistics do not start tasks.

dashboard_1.title: Shortcuts
dashboard_1.body: Open the matching page from a summary card; Enter works too. Expand or collapse navigation and reopen this guide at any time.

dashboard_2.title: Charts and resources
dashboard_2.body: Charts summarize existing data. Resource notices use available resources; assess concurrency with task state and resource checks.

attackAlert_0.title: Page purpose
attackAlert_0.body: Inspect attack alerts and their sources.

attackAlert_1.title: Type, severity and source filters
attackAlert_1.body: Type and severity filter automatically. Search a source IP with Enter or Query; clear conditions to broaden results.

attackAlert_2.title: Alert records and provenance
attackAlert_2.body: Inspect target, source, count, confidence and severity. Select a source IP for its records and use details to inspect evidence.

attackAlert_3.title: Refresh and alert counters
attackAlert_3.body: Refresh reloads alerts and counters. Details show collected request evidence; Trace looks up records for the source IP.

tasks_0.title: Page purpose
tasks_0.body: Manage scan task status and outputs.

tasks_1.title: Filter and reset
tasks_1.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

tasks_2.title: Create and execution actions
tasks_2.body: New opens task configuration. Stop, Continue or Restart depend on state. Select tasks before bulk stop and check the confirmation before stopping or restarting.

tasks_3.title: Details and deletion scope
tasks_3.body: Details show results. The deletion dialog separately controls collected assets and stopping/deleting associated AI sessions. Task-only deletion preserves assets; discovered findings survive session removal.

taskCreate_0.title: Page purpose
taskCreate_0.body: Create a scan task for an authorized scope.

taskCreate_1.title: Name, policy and target
taskCreate_1.body: Name the task, select an existing policy and choose direct targets, an asset engine or an organization. Target inputs depend on type. Configure required data sources first.

taskCreate_2.title: Scope and options
taskCreate_2.body: Review targets, exclusions, scan options and resource hints. The chosen policy controls automatic AI testing; red team mode requires acknowledgment.

taskCreate_3.title: Submit the task
taskCreate_3.body: After submitting, check live status in the task list. Complete required fields and use the displayed format for multiple targets.

policy_1.title: Create and edit
policy_1.body: New opens policy configuration. Edit per row to change an existing policy; check dependent schedules before deletion.

policy_2.title: Filter and reset
policy_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

policy_3.title: Policies and row actions
policy_3.body: Search by name and query/reset. Edit or confirm deletion per row. This list offers no copy or bulk-selection action.

taskSchedule_0.title: Page purpose
taskSchedule_0.body: Schedule task runs; inspect actual runs in the task list.

taskSchedule_1.title: Basic settings
taskSchedule_1.body: Enter the name, policy, schedule and preferred/optional backup/supervisory models first. Next opens the target step.

taskSchedule_2.title: Filter and reset
taskSchedule_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

taskSchedule_3.title: Schedule row actions
taskSchedule_3.body: Pause, recover or confirm deletion per schedule row. One-time and recurring schedules show their current state; pagination changes the view only.

taskSchedule_4.title: Asset group and targets
taskSchedule_4.body: An optional asset group fills the editable target field. Enter targets directly or append and modify them. Previous returns to the model and scheduling settings.

pentest_0.title: Sessions and creation source
pentest_0.body: View system, manual and workgroup sessions. The source indicates how the session was created, separate from status, target, model and usage.

pentest_1.title: Filter and reset
pentest_1.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

pentest_2.title: New session and console
pentest_2.body: Create through the console. Details shows summaries; Console opens interaction. A manual whiteboard without a target stays on standby.

pentest_3.title: Records and bulk actions
pentest_3.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

pentest_4.title: Stop, resume and delete
pentest_4.body: Stop takes precedence over late approval and unattended continuation. Review errors before resuming; deletion removes the confirmed session and space.

pentestConsole_0.title: Page purpose
pentestConsole_0.body: Choose a session card to enter the console; automatic-session takeover needs one initial acknowledgment.

pentestConsole_1.title: Filter, create and session cards
pentestConsole_1.body: Filter by name, state or dates, or open a session key. Creation selects target, model and mode; red-team mode requires acknowledgement. The first card metric is context space; the final storage-space metric is file usage in MB.

pentestConsole_2.title: Commands and uploads
pentestConsole_2.body: Send instructions from the composer; upload shows progress and attaches files to this session. Stop running work as needed and take over an automatic session to interact. Input and uploads are disabled in unattended mode.

pentestConsole_3.title: Full authorization and unattended mode
pentestConsole_3.body: Only two switches sit beside Upload. Full authorization uses skills alone; when off, suspected high-risk requests need review. Unattended mode inherits the current authorization setting: full authorization on means authorized operation; otherwise mode guards apply. Its switch and banner turn yellow; switching off cancels it.

pentestConsole_4.title: Approvals, packets and history
pentestConsole_4.body: Pending reviews appear above input. Inspect the full packet and verdict, then allow or block; unresolved requests expire after 30 seconds. AI can do other work. Approval sends the immutable packet. Reapply from history; unknown outcomes are not automatically replayed.

pentestConsole_5.title: Attack surface and session space
pentestConsole_5.body: The left panel lists ports, endpoints, leads and findings; open a finding for evidence. Session space browses scripts, downloads and images with preview/download, restricted to authorized session files.

pentestConsole_6.title: Tools, AI browser and Burps
pentestConsole_6.body: Expand tool cards for arguments/results. The AI browser and yellow Burps panels are draggable. Burps provides streaming history, filters, encoding views, HTTP edit/replay and confirmed clearing, without deleting session messages.

miniapp_0.title: Page purpose
miniapp_0.body: Unpack and audit authorized local miniapp packages.

miniapp_1.title: Upload a folder and unpack
miniapp_1.body: Select a wx-prefixed AppID folder containing main/subpackage .wxapkg files. Check progress; Path Help lists copyable cache locations. Inspect the message if the unpacker is unavailable or fails.

miniapp_2.title: History, file selection and launch
miniapp_2.body: Select history to inspect an unpacked miniapp, then select its package and open Launch. Each package creates one session. Browsing history does not run a task; deletion requires confirmation.

appPentest_0.title: Page purpose
appPentest_0.body: Use Watchtower Link to route selected app traffic to the platform.

appPentest_1.title: Phone and connection
appPentest_1.body: Install/update Link and select USB/ADB or wireless. USB requires Android permission; use a reachable peer address on Windows. A disconnected state means capture is not active.

appPentest_2.title: Egress, certificate and capture
appPentest_2.body: Direct egress is default; platform egress is optional. Follow HTTPS certificate installation instructions. Pinning or missing trust can prevent plaintext capture. Without accessibility, manually operate app features.

appPentest_3.title: Device traffic and AI sessions
appPentest_3.body: Add Device combines wired and wireless setup. Configure the connection, then Search to open the radar. Pairing method uses device reports; offline records do not count as online. Set egress and the target on the phone. Copy the native wireless gateway URL; Web wired access uses the downloaded helper.

probeManage_0.title: Page purpose
probeManage_0.body: Manage available probes and deployment status.

probeManage_1.title: Probe, agent and blue-team tabs
probeManage_1.body: Create a probe with name, reachable address, port and key; build/download/check per row. Agent creation selects bound probes, platform and connection settings. The blue-team tab currently displays a development notice.

probeManage_2.title: Build artifacts and status
probeManage_2.body: Download becomes available after a row is built. Check/Status reads deployed connectivity. There is no bulk selection; a build artifact is not deployment confirmation.

probeManage_3.title: Refresh and delete
probeManage_3.body: Refresh reads existing records. Confirm deletion per configuration row. Leaving this page does not uninstall deployed probes or agents.

aiConfig_0.title: Page purpose
aiConfig_0.body: Manage model connections, mode prompts and AI settings.

aiConfig_1.title: Model connection and testing
aiConfig_1.body: Add/edit provider type, display name, exact model, endpoint and credentials. Saving, activation and connectivity tests are separate; tests may make actual API calls.

aiConfig_2.title: Edit and reset prompts
aiConfig_2.body: All listed prompts are editable after acknowledging effects on future AI behavior. Reset restores current-version default text after confirmation and preserves model settings.

aiConfig_3.title: Enable and scope
aiConfig_3.body: Check each prompt’s scene and enabled state. Saved content is read by the corresponding mode or tool; unsaved editor text does not take effect.

vulnCenter_0.title: Page purpose
vulnCenter_0.body: Inspect verified findings and unverified leads.

vulnCenter_1.title: Filter and reset
vulnCenter_1.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

vulnCenter_2.title: Evidence and status
vulnCenter_2.body: Inspect endpoint, type, source session and evidence. The same endpoint and vulnerability are unique; different vulnerabilities remain separate. Leads require actual validation. Source categories are AI assessment, kernel scan and workgroup. Kernel combines PoC/Nuclei; Workgroup covers shared records restored locally.

vulnCenter_3.title: Generate finding reports
vulnCenter_3.body: Choose a template for a finding, session or task. Defaults are the original built-in templates; custom templates are selectable. Preview/edit/export the result in Report editor.

vulnCenter_4.title: Records and bulk actions
vulnCenter_4.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

reportEdit_0.title: Page purpose
reportEdit_0.body: Manage task, session and finding reports and custom templates.

reportEdit_1.title: Choose the report level and source
reportEdit_1.body: Every generation button opens a searchable, paginated source picker. Select one task, session or finding, then choose the template, title and optional AI completion. Internal IDs are not typed. Template-row generation uses the same flow; existing manual report edits remain protected.

reportEdit_2.title: Generate, preview and edit
reportEdit_2.body: Choose a template to generate a report and preview existing reports. Save edited content before exporting. AI-assisted organization may use the configured model.

reportEdit_3.title: Manual marking and AI learning
reportEdit_3.body: Create a report template, upload Word, then choose manual marking or AI learning. Manual marking edits the original document with natural language and tags; learning can call a model. Both require review. Existing text templates remain editable.

poc_1.title: Import and sync
poc_1.body: Import a script or a ZIP batch. Download the template to check entry/argument requirements. Confirm built-in sync. Importing alone does not establish script safety or successful verification.

poc_2.title: Filter and reset
poc_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

poc_3.title: Records and bulk actions
poc_3.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

poc_4.title: Delete and clear
poc_4.body: Deletion affects selected items; clearing affects the whole list and needs confirmation. Run verification through authorized tasks.

vulnIntel_0.title: Page purpose
vulnIntel_0.body: Inspect central and local vulnerability intelligence.

vulnIntel_1.title: Filter and reset
vulnIntel_1.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

vulnIntel_2.title: Identifiers and publishers
vulnIntel_2.body: Keep CVE where available; otherwise use internal WTI-year/month-sequence identifiers. Linked titles open the publisher. No source means no fabricated link.

vulnIntel_3.title: Pull, validate and notify
vulnIntel_3.body: Pull intelligence and inspect PoC/execution availability. High-risk notifications are grouped by collection run. Intelligence does not prove a target is vulnerable.

attackChain_0.title: Sessions and attack chains
attackChain_0.body: Locate records by session, target and organization. Targets branch to independent findings; explicit parent steps or findings create continuations. Intranet entry points are labelled separately.

attackChain_1.title: Session and target filters
attackChain_1.body: Enter a source session ID, target text, organization or state and search. Reset clears filters. Target text is treated literally, not as a regular expression; source columns and node details support traceability.

attackChain_2.title: Records and bulk actions
attackChain_2.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

attackChain_3.title: Branch graph and source details
attackChain_3.body: Open a graph preview to pan, zoom and inspect targets, sessions and references in a movable dialog. Independent findings branch from targets; chronology alone does not imply causation. The console reuses this same graph component.

intel_0.title: Page purpose
intel_0.body: Browse asset instances, system knowledge, code audits, reports and organizations.

intel_1.title: Categories and objects
intel_1.body: Switch knowledge categories and query the current one. Counts across categories are not one shared result.

intel_2.title: Filter and reset
intel_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

intel_3.title: Records and bulk actions
intel_3.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

intel_4.title: Report and organization links
intel_4.body: Inspect report text/findings. Organization view summarizes systems, subdomains, intelligence and chains; links depend on source data.

unitView_0.title: Page purpose
unitView_0.body: Inspect assets, findings, reports and chains by organization.

unitView_1.title: Unit search and sorting
unitView_1.body: Typing a unit name filters immediately. Sort by assessment time or finding count; clear the name to show all units.

unitView_2.title: Detail categories
unitView_2.body: Select an organization and switch findings, reports, chains, subdomains and intelligence. Open records for details.

unitView_3.title: Unit selection and related cleanup
unitView_3.body: Open details from a unit card. Select cards or Select All on Page for bulk deletion. Check units and related-data scope in the confirmation; data deletion cannot undo actions executed on a target.

search_0.title: Local asset search
search_0.body: Search assets already collected by this instance. Source discovery and new scans are configured in New Task; these filters read existing results.

search_1.title: Eight asset collections and details
search_1.body: Choose Sites, Domains, IPs, URLs, Certificates, Services, File Leaks or WIH. Details show the raw record; sites also provide screenshots and tag management.

search_2.title: Filter and reset
search_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

search_3.title: Export, select and delete
search_3.body: CSV export follows the current collection and filters. Select All can include all matching results across pages. Confirm deletion after checking the selected count and filter scope.

assetGroups_1.title: Create a group and its scope
assetGroups_1.body: Enter name, scope, exclusions and Domain/IP type. Open row details to manage members. This list has no group-edit action.

assetGroups_2.title: Filter and reset
assetGroups_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

assetGroups_3.title: Group row actions
assetGroups_3.body: Open details per row to inspect members. Confirmed deletion applies to that group. Copy scope and exclusions directly.

assetGroupDetail_0.title: Page purpose
assetGroupDetail_0.body: Inspect group domains, IPs, sites and WIH.

assetGroupDetail_1.title: Categories and members
assetGroupDetail_1.body: Switch asset categories and query members. Add/remove/export applies to the current category.

assetGroupDetail_2.title: Filter and reset
assetGroupDetail_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

assetGroupDetail_3.title: Records and bulk actions
assetGroupDetail_3.body: Open a title or Details to inspect a record. Bulk actions apply to selected rows; verify the objects in the confirmation. Refresh and pagination only update the view.

assetMonitor_1.title: Domain, site and WIH monitoring
assetMonitor_1.body: Choose a monitor type and existing asset group; domain monitoring also requires domains. Empty names are generated automatically. Set the interval in hours, with a minimum of six.

assetMonitor_2.title: Filter and reset
assetMonitor_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

assetMonitor_3.title: Monitor records and row actions
assetMonitor_3.body: Inspect interval, state, run count and next execution time. Confirm Stop, Recover or Delete per row. This table has no bulk selection or policy selector.

assetMonitor_4.title: Monitor results and tasks
assetMonitor_4.body: Stop/Recover controls subsequent monitoring. Inspect collected results in asset groups and manage executing jobs in the task list.

githubTasks_0.title: Page purpose
githubTasks_0.body: Manage code search tasks and their results.

githubTasks_1.title: Create a code-search task
githubTasks_1.body: Submit a name and GitHub search keywords. Configure source credentials in API Keys. Searching consumes GitHub API quota.

githubTasks_2.title: Filter and reset
githubTasks_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

githubTasks_3.title: Results, stop and delete
githubTasks_3.body: Open results per row. Confirm Stop for running tasks or Delete for a record. There is no bulk selection or scan-policy selector.

githubMonitor_0.title: Page purpose
githubMonitor_0.body: Manage code monitoring schedules and their results.

githubMonitor_1.title: Create or edit code monitoring
githubMonitor_1.body: Enter monitor name, GitHub keywords and Cron. Edit a row to change an existing monitor and check the current time zone.

githubMonitor_2.title: Filter and reset
githubMonitor_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

githubMonitor_3.title: Results and monitoring state
githubMonitor_3.body: View results, edit and confirm Stop/Recover or Delete per row. There is no bulk selection. Stopping future monitoring does not clear historical search results.

userManage_0.title: Page purpose
userManage_0.body: Administrators manage this instance’s users, roles and permissions.

userManage_1.title: Users and roles
userManage_1.body: Switch users/roles and use row actions to create, edit, disable or reset passwords. Control Keys, peer memberships and user accounts are separate credentials.

userManage_2.title: Permissions and save
userManage_2.body: Select required read/write permissions and save. Check active work and account usage before deletion/disable.

userManage_3.title: User and role row actions
userManage_3.body: Edit, disable/enable or confirm deletion per user. An empty password keeps it unchanged. Edit/delete custom roles; inspect permissions for built-in roles. There is no bulk selection.

proxy_0.title: Page purpose
proxy_0.body: Configure instance proxy egress and nodes.

proxy_1.title: Subscriptions and kernel nodes
proxy_1.body: Expand the kernel proxy, import a subscription URL or upload YAML and activate a profile. Select nodes manually or use automatic selection. Save port and DNS settings separately.

proxy_2.title: Direct mode, sources and egress
proxy_2.body: Unconfigured systems default to direct. Smart may be unbound, custom, kernel or pool; custom requires a selected entry. Explicit kernel selection/save performs a fresh check. Failure explains why and changes only the draft to direct; saved settings remain unchanged until Save.

proxy_3.title: Public proxy pool and bulk actions
proxy_3.body: Expand the public pool, configure crawl queries and save. Refresh, Crawl and Verify are separate actions. Pool-table selection enables bulk verify, enable/disable or confirmed delete; check availability first.

networkCheck_0.title: Page purpose
networkCheck_0.body: Check DNS, connectivity, proxy and network quality.

networkCheck_1.title: Health check and individual tests
networkCheck_1.body: Run Health Check to sample link, egress, DNS, dependencies and proxy. Use the individual Ping/resolution controls below for a target and count. Wait for results while the check runs.

networkCheck_2.title: Results and suggestions
networkCheck_2.body: Expand failures for causes/timing. Scores represent a sample; fix issues and recheck rather than treating them as all-day reliability proof.

apiKeys_0.title: Page purpose
apiKeys_0.body: Configure asset-source, notification and other API credentials. The platform ID is the activation JWT uid and is read-only. The push threshold appears before Webhook fields, and messages include a W-linux/W-win source.

apiKeys_1.title: Categories and credentials
apiKeys_1.body: Fill required service fields using password inputs for secrets. Leave unused sources blank and never share these as group invitations.

apiKeys_2.title: Enable, save and refresh
apiKeys_2.body: After changing source switches or fields, select Save All. Refresh prompts about unsaved edits. Get opens the source website; it is not a connection test.

logs_0.title: Page purpose
logs_0.body: Inspect runtime logs and component errors.

logs_1.title: Filters and full details
logs_1.body: Query/reset severity, process, module or keyword. Open a row detail drawer for full logs and exception traces. Refresh reads counters and records.

logs_2.title: Selection, clear and retention
logs_2.body: Select rows and confirm deletion of selected logs. Clear applies to all logs. Retention sets days per category; preserve evidence needed for diagnosis.

accessLog_1.title: All access and writes
accessLog_1.body: Switch all access or writes, and narrow by user, endpoint, status or date.

accessLog_2.title: Filter and reset
accessLog_2.body: Enter filters, then use Query or Search. Reset clears filters without deleting records. Scroll within the table to see more columns.

accessLog_3.title: Access records and retention
accessLog_3.body: Page through time, user, path, status, IP and elapsed time. Refresh or set retention at the top right. This table does not offer bulk deletion.

guardLog_0.title: Page purpose
guardLog_0.body: Traffic log records platform-observable session traffic, including allowed requests.

guardLog_1.title: Session ID and filters
guardLog_1.body: Filter by full session ID with method, action, address and time. Permissions limit visible sessions.

guardLog_2.title: Request, response and encoding
guardLog_2.body: Click a traffic row for request/response interaction, with UTF-8, GBK, Hex or Base64 views. Blocked requests show Blocked. Captured packets up to 1 MiB combined are retained and scrollable. Over-budget/window captures are marked; TLS tunnels still have metadata and Burps is independent.

guardLog_3.title: Capacity, retention and cleanup
guardLog_3.body: Configure capacity and the default 30-day retention. Age/capacity pruning removes old records. Filters do not limit cleanup; retain needed evidence before changing settings.

controlSync_0.title: Page purpose
controlSync_0.body: MCP control and data sync are separate; their credentials are not interchangeable.

controlSync_1.title: Create and manage control Keys
controlSync_1.body: On the Control Key tab, Create from the Key card’s right-hand button, with name, finite expiry and allowed operations. Administrators only. Revoke disables immediately; confirm deletion. Plaintext Keys are not recovered.

controlSync_2.title: HTTP and MCP access
controlSync_2.body: On the Control Key tab, Give another AI the HTTP guide URL and Key, or use the dedicated endpoint in an MCP client. Replace example IPs with a caller-reachable address.

controlSync_3.title: Receiver pairing links
controlSync_3.body: Enter a reachable IP or domain. Windows adds the receiver port automatically; explicit ports are accepted. Incomplete fields show a prompt. Node mode requires an endpoint, fingerprint and credential. Choose limited validity and categories before generating a link; no migration starts yet.

controlSync_4.title: Paste, connect and confirm
controlSync_4.body: The initiator pastes the link to fill editable address/Key, then connects. Both sides confirm in dialogs. The initiator polls; reverse connectivity is not required. Reuse history targets and revoke/delete connections.

controlSync_5.title: One record per sync operation
controlSync_5.body: Click a record summary for its progress, stage, categories and results. Completed, failed, rejected or expired records can be removed; active or pending operations cannot. Imported business data and protocol retry receipts remain.

collaboration_0.title: Page purpose
collaboration_0.body: Cross-Web/Windows workgroups provide a shared room and private two-member rooms.

collaboration_1.title: Create and invite
collaboration_1.body: Create from the list’s right-hand button with a reachable host address. Invitations default to no expiry, with optional expiry, member cap and approval. Share the credential-bearing link only with intended members.

collaboration_2.title: Join and approval
collaboration_2.body: Paste into Join to fill editable address/Key. Connect explicitly and wait while this client polls. The host approves/rejects/removes from Members. Permanent invitations do not remove membership expiry.

collaboration_3.title: Shared, direct and messages
collaboration_3.body: The shared room is visible to active members; direct rooms only to both participants. Drafts are per room and messages show source clients. Load older messages upward.

collaboration_4.title: Findings, reports and handoff
collaboration_4.body: Share existing findings, reports or complete sessions to the current room. Preview received packages. Restoring selects a local model and creates a standby session without starting the original.

collaboration_5.title: Rotate, close and delete
collaboration_5.body: Rotating invalidates old invitation Keys while existing members keep their own credentials. Deleting a hosted group closes new access; deleting a joined link removes the local connection and preserves shared evidence.

systemExtension_0.title: Page purpose
systemExtension_0.body: Manage AI tools, kernel tools and private/cloud extensions.

systemExtension_1.title: Type and name filters
systemExtension_1.body: Filter AI/kernel tools independently by function or name. Reset only clears filters. Cards show entry, parameters and availability.

systemExtension_2.title: Tool documentation
systemExtension_2.body: Click a tool card to read its standard documentation. Short descriptions open in a centered modal and long descriptions use a drawer. Enable, check and remove are separate actions.

systemExtension_3.title: Cloud verification and isolation
systemExtension_3.body: Cloud requires a code sent to your registered email, up to five submissions/day and 300 MiB/package. Pending and approved packages remain isolated. Upload does not publish/enable; local stays private.

systemExtension_4.title: Store, enablement and logs
systemExtension_4.body: The store offers compatible packages. Read documentation before install/enable. Cards provide details, update checks and deletion. Use runtime logs for failures.

aiTools_0.title: Page purpose
aiTools_0.body: Inspect callable AI tools and parameter contracts.

aiTools_1.title: Capabilities and arguments
aiTools_1.body: Expand tools for docs, arguments and availability. Calling also depends on tool configuration, session mode and permissions.

manual_0.title: Page purpose
manual_0.body: Read the user manual and FAQ.

manual_1.title: Sections and documentation
manual_1.body: Use sections for installation, configuration, tasks, console and extensions. Page guides explain operation; the manual holds fuller contracts.

activation_0.title: Page purpose
activation_0.body: Inspect activation state/expiry and manage this instance’s license. The platform ID is the activation JWT uid and is read-only. The push threshold appears before Webhook fields, and messages include a W-linux/W-win source.

activation_1.title: Credential and platform number
activation_1.body: The read-only platform number below the credential comes from the current JWT uid. Open Activate or Renew to paste a credential in its dialog. Keep credentials out of reports.

activation_2.title: Status and source
activation_2.body: Inspect authoritative active/expired/revoked state. Obtain renewed credentials from the source service, then refresh and verify dates.

updateCheck_0.title: Page purpose
updateCheck_0.body: Inspect and apply adjacent signed platform updates.

updateCheck_1.title: Check and version order
updateCheck_1.body: Check latest and read changes. Current version is not artificially sorted first. Web/Windows use separate channels; upgrade and rollback are adjacent.

updateCheck_2.title: Update, progress and resume
updateCheck_2.body: Finish relevant work, then start. Watch download, verification, apply and restart. Resume interrupted chains without deleting locks/cache; the native Windows app may reopen.

updateCheck_3.title: Rollback and same-version repair
updateCheck_3.body: Rollback follows adjacent prepared versions above the minimum. Same-version repair performs full checks. The 175 minimum remains; test builds are not formal releases.

changelog_0.title: Local changelog
changelog_0.body: History is read from files delivered with the installed version, without fetching remote history. System updates open by default; switch to patch updates for fixes to existing features.

changelog_1.title: System and patch records
changelog_1.body: Feature additions/removals belong to system versions; existing-feature fixes belong to patches. Patch serials stay hidden in the main version label. Test iterations are development builds, not formal releases.

developer_1.title: Project and participation
developer_1.body: Use available website, GitHub or contribution links. External links leave this instance. Do not post credentials or customer data publicly.

title: Operation guide
unavailable: This operation is inside the relevant tab, detail or dialog, or needs data/permission. The guide does not click, submit or start work for you.
mascot: Whale guide points out the controls

taskDetail_0.title: Task details
taskDetail_0.body: This page summarizes one task, its result counts and enabled options.

taskDetail_1.title: Identity, state and targets
taskDetail_1.body: Copy the task ID or full target; check start/end time and duration. Source queries appear when available.

taskDetail_2.title: Open task results
taskDetail_2.body: Select View below a domain, IP, site, URL or WIH count. Asset search opens filtered by this task ID. Zero indicates no results of that type.

taskDetail_3.title: Enabled task options
taskDetail_3.body: This section displays the enabled options saved with the task. Manage task execution in the task list; configure future scans in policies or task creation.

taskDetail_4.title: Return to tasks
taskDetail_4.body: Return to the list to view or manage tasks. Leaving this page does not stop execution.

fingerprint_0.title: Fingerprint entry
fingerprint_0.body: This page explains where fingerprint capabilities live. Asset-instance fingerprints and system knowledge are available in Intelligence.

fingerprint_1.title: Open Intelligence
fingerprint_1.body: Select the Intelligence button and choose asset instances or system knowledge to inspect collected fingerprints.

pentestDetail_0.title: Session details
pentestDetail_0.body: Inspect session information, results, tool logs and dialogue. Manual standby is distinct from failures requiring attention.

pentestDetail_1.title: Identity and console
pentestDetail_1.body: Copy the session ID or open its console beside the session key. Check the model, mode, target, source task and latest error.

pentestDetail_2.title: Refresh and state actions
pentestDetail_2.body: Refresh reads current information. Eligible automatic sessions offer Start or Resume; continue manual sessions in the console. Back leaves this page.

pentestDetail_3.title: Result narrative
pentestDetail_3.body: Read the result narrative when present. If it is empty, inspect status and history; an empty result is not verification.

pentestDetail_4.title: Tools and dialogue
pentestDetail_4.body: Expand tool logs for arguments and results. Dialogue records load from the server on demand. Expanding panels does not send AI instructions.

pentestLive_0.title: Live observation
pentestLive_0.body: This page observes a session without sending instructions. Stream connection and execution state are separate; observation ending does not imply task failure.

pentestLive_1.title: Session and connection state
pentestLive_1.body: Manual standby, running, unattended mode and errors have distinct labels and colors. Reopen after observation closes to read the latest snapshot.

pentestLive_2.title: Counters and surface
pentestLive_2.body: Counters show rounds, tokens, tools and findings. The surface refresh reads existing context without starting a scan.

pentestLive_3.title: Inspect tool results
pentestLive_3.body: Expand a tool header for its arguments and result. Thought text arrives with the observation stream. Open details to enter the interactive console using the session key.

pentestLive_4.title: Details and back
pentestLive_4.body: Open details or return to the session list at the top right. These links navigate without stopping execution.

policyEdit_0.title: Policy configuration
policyEdit_0.body: Configure reusable collection, scan and AI defaults. Changes affect future tasks after saving.

policyEdit_1.title: Collection mode and sources
policyEdit_1.body: Single-target and multiple-source modes show different inputs. Multiple-source collection requires configured sources.

policyEdit_2.title: DNS, ports and sites
policyEdit_2.body: Configure DNS dictionaries/resolvers, ports, service detection, site collection and validation by section. Expand optional dictionaries; empty values use defaults.

policyEdit_3.title: Automatic AI assessment
policyEdit_3.body: The yellow option remains noticeable. Enabling it reveals mode, deduplication and scope settings; choose a model when creating a task.

policyEdit_4.title: Mode and red-team acknowledgement
policyEdit_4.body: Enable automatic AI before selecting a mode. Red-team selection requires acknowledgement; cancelling preserves the previous mode.

policyEdit_5.title: Scope drift and unrestricted
policyEdit_5.body: Choose no, light, moderate or unrestricted scope drift in the automatic AI section. Unrestricted broadens exploration for the task.

policyEdit_6.title: Validation and password-check plugins
policyEdit_6.body: Search and move required plugins into the enabled list. Available entries come from installed kernel tools.

policyEdit_7.title: Save, back and dependencies
policyEdit_7.body: Saving checks required configuration and stores the policy. Leaving with unsaved changes prompts before discarding.

attackAlert_4.title: Ban and unban
attackAlert_4.body: Confirm Ban per alert. The ban list shows expiry and Unban. Adding an IP to the allowlist also removes its ban; check the source first.

attackAlert_5.title: Allowlist management
attackAlert_5.body: Enter an IP to add it or confirm removal per row. Refresh only reads the list. This setting affects the platform’s own alert protection.

tasks_4.title: Asset synchronization and reports
tasks_4.body: Synchronize in a task row selects an asset group for collected results. Report selects a task template. Inspect messages for empty results or unavailable templates.

tasks_5.title: Clean orphaned assets
tasks_5.body: Check counts and provenance before confirming cleanup of assets left by deleted tasks. Cleanup cannot proceed when task records cannot be read safely.

taskCreate_4.title: Primary/backup model and context
taskCreate_4.body: AI-enabled policies reveal primary/backup model and per-session context settings. Backup must use the same protocol. Native, global-default or explicit budgets apply to this task.

taskCreate_5.title: Egress and observer
taskCreate_5.body: AI options select primary/fallback egress. An optional observer uses its chosen model and adds model calls. Unconfigured egress choices are unavailable.

taskCreate_6.title: Exclusions and temporary intelligence
taskCreate_6.body: The no-assessment list skips automatic AI dispatch. Temporary intelligence can target a unit, host or the whole task; check its content and scope before submission.

taskCreate_7.title: CSV batch and priority
taskCreate_7.body: Download the CSV template, fill it and upload to create tasks sharing the policy. Set single-task priority in the form. Check submission results in the task list.

networkCheck_3.title: Custom and built-in DNS
networkCheck_3.body: After adding, editing or removing custom DNS, select Save Custom. The collapsible built-in DNS list is read-only and is not changed by this save.

apiKeys_3.title: Notifications and intelligence push
apiKeys_3.body: Notification sources can set severity and intelligence push. Save them with other fields using Save All. Newly added high-severity intelligence is grouped by collection batch.

logs_3.title: Reports and developer replies
logs_3.body: Select logs and open Upload to Cloud. Review the attached ownership/version/egress information and description before submitting. My Reports shows this account’s submissions and replies.

aiConfig_4.title: Default model and global settings
aiConfig_4.body: Save the default model, timeout, source directory and concurrency limit. Zero concurrency uses resource recommendations; sessions with locked models keep their choices.

aiConfig_5.title: Token totals and expansion
aiConfig_5.body: Collapsed by default: calls, total tokens, input/output and failed calls stay visible. Expand for model and stage breakdowns. Refresh reads statistics without calling a model; global parameters keep their layout.

aiConfig_6.title: Explicit model SKILL bindings
aiConfig_6.body: Add a binding, choose a uniquely named configured model and required built-in stages, upload the bundle and select its entry. Both model name and stage must match. Guard bindings require risk confirmation. Legacy unscoped bindings need stages; built-in tool and safety constraints remain.

proxy_4.title: Custom proxies
proxy_4.body: Expand Custom Proxies to add/edit connection settings. Enable, test or confirm deletion per row. Select model ingress proxies in AI Configuration.

proxy_5.title: Health and traffic counters
proxy_5.body: Inspect kernel health, current egress and traffic totals. View counters by subscription/node. Reset requires confirmation and does not delete proxy configuration.

proxy_6.title: Logs and unsaved changes
proxy_6.body: Expand and refresh logs. Mode, kernel and pool settings have separate saves; saving one does not mark the others saved. Refresh preserves drafts. Leaving lets you keep or discard unsaved settings and subscription/YAML input.

assetGroups_4.title: Create a pentest task
assetGroups_4.body: Open Create pentest task from a group row, review its scope and choose a policy with automatic AI testing after scanning. Cancel creates nothing; only final submission starts task orchestration, without directly creating a console session.

assetGroupDetail_4.title: Group task entry
assetGroupDetail_4.body: The right-side button opens the task draft for this group. Entire ranges overlapping exclusions are visibly omitted. Asset read and task write permissions are required; a scope changed since preview must be reviewed again.

collaborationWorkspace_0.title: Independent workspace
collaborationWorkspace_0.body: Only the current workspace is shown here. Back returns to the workgroup list. Operations remain scoped to this group.

collaborationWorkspace_1.title: Shared and direct rooms
collaborationWorkspace_1.body: The shared room is visible to approved members. A direct room is private to its two participants. Downloading a message does not mark it read.

collaborationWorkspace_2.title: Members and applications
collaborationWorkspace_2.body: Members and join/rename applications are separate. Only the host approves membership, removes members and approves names. Co-hosts maintain service.

collaborationWorkspace_3.title: Workspace names and IDs
collaborationWorkspace_3.body: Each member has a unique eight-character ID and workspace name. Members request renames; the host can rename directly. Encryption identity does not change.

collaborationWorkspace_4.title: Share materials
collaborationWorkspace_4.body: Share findings, reports or a complete inactive session package. Preview before restoring; restoration does not auto-execute. Individual files must not exceed 20 MiB.

collaborationWorkspace_5.title: Maintenance nodes and cached delivery
collaborationWorkspace_5.body: The host downloads the generic program, adds workspace nodes and views five-second health samples in Maintenance nodes. Cache and delivery separately selects the node and realtime/hosted policy. Members receive no administration credential.

collaborationWorkspace_6.title: Back and unread state
collaborationWorkspace_6.body: Workgroup and sidebar badges show incoming messages outside the workspace. Viewing the relevant room and scrolling to the latest messages marks it read.

collaborationWorkspace_7.title: Management, service and route
collaborationWorkspace_7.body: The administrative host controls approvals and settings. A member must opt in and receive approval before its prepared co-host can serve public data. See the reachable service and last verified path here. With no reachable host or co-host, live service is offline and local pending data stays intact.

controlSync_6.title: Isolated node routing
controlSync_6.body: Enter the node URL, TLS fingerprint and administration credential. The invitation excludes administration access. Each pairing has a separate realm. Paste the complete invitation on the initiator to select this route; interruptions retain the original plan and verified chunks. The generic node starts without an IP argument, on7443 by default. The connecting platform enters its reachable address and verifies its fingerprint.

miniapp_3.title: Interaction and models
miniapp_3.body: Standard is the default intensity. Unattended runs automatically; human-led waits for your messages. The preferred model starts from the global default; backup is off and offers other models of the same protocol. Review these options before launching.

taskSchedule_5.title: Group targets and AI models
taskSchedule_5.body: Enter targets or choose an asset group. Submission saves its authoritative target snapshot with exclusions respected. Preferred uses the default; backup and supervision start disabled. Supervision may use an independent model. AI options apply only when the policy enables automatic AI.

reportEdit_4.title: New report template
reportEdit_4.body: Choose manual annotation or AI learning in New report template. Both require a base Word file. Annotate paragraphs and table cells directly while retaining layout and images. Both require review and confirmation. Existing text templates remain editable.

apiKeys_4.title: Notification threshold and source
apiKeys_4.body: Above Webhook in the alert card, set the threshold and view the read-only platform number. Notifications identify their source with W-linux/W-win and that number. Save all after editing the threshold.

attackAlert_6.title: Automatic collection status
attackAlert_6.body: The banner describes automatic log collection support. Native Windows and non-Docker environments do not report a running collector. Docker read failures or expired leases remain visible. Refresh reads shared status and existing alerts.

collaboration_8.title: Workspace attachments
collaboration_8.body: Select files below the input, remove pending files if needed, then Send with or without text. Files use the current group/direct recipients, encrypted outbox and node cache. Older participants must update. Downloads recheck access and files are never executed by the platform.
